To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
angiotensin stimulates H+-ATPs in CNT and CCD intercalated cells.
angiotensin stimulates H+-ATPs in intercalated cells from CNT/CC and that this may be a mechanism for regulation of bicarbonate secretion and chloride absorption in this nephron region.

angiotensin stimulates H+-ATPs in CNT/CD intercalated cells in an AT1-receptor and microtubule dependent manner, and that this stimulation of H+-ATPs may contribute to the stimulation of bicarbonate secretion by angiotensin in this nephron region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of H+-ATpases in the kidney.
the regulation of acid-base transport by the connecting tubules and the early cortical collecting ducts (CNT/CCD), which are the final segment of the nephron in the mammalian kidney.
the regulation of H+-ATPSes in the kidney and the regulation of acid-base homeostasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

angiotensin 2 (AT2) stimulates the H+-ATP-ase in intercalated cells in the connecting tubule and the cortical collecting duct, which is important for the regulation of bicarbonate secretion and chloride reabsorption in this nephron section.
the effect of angio II on H+ATPases is mediated by the microtubular system, which is consistent with the known role of microtubules in the regulation of H+ATPase activity.
angiotensin stimulates H+-ATPAse activity in intercalated cells in CNT and early CCD, and that this effect is mediated via AT1-receptors, and is dependent on an intact microturbular network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
angiotensin 2 regulates H+-ATP activity in the connecting tubule and early cortical collecting tubules.
angiotensin-II stimulates chloride absorption and bicarb secretion in the CNT/CC by stimulating pendrin and H+-ATP.

angiotensin 2 stimulates H+ATPase activity in intercalated cells from isolated connecting tubules and CCDs and this may contribute to the stimulation of chloride absorption and/or bicarbonate secretion in these nephron segments.
The main takeaway from our work is that

angiotensin-II can increase the activity of the H+-ATP pump, and this is important because the H+-ATp pump is the primary source of energy for the chloride transporter pendrin in intercalated cells of the connecting tubule and early cortical collecting tubule.
angiotensin 2 increases H+ ATPase in intercalated cells of CNT/CCDS.
angiotensin-II stimulates H+-ATPs in CNT and CCD intercalated cells in a microtubule dependent manner, and this may contribute to the stimulation of bicarbonate secretion by these cells.
